methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $30M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Cemvita is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Moji and Tara Karimi that has raised $30M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private-stage peers and one public company (LNZA) operating in the Climate & Energy sector, including stage-adjacent businesses like KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $30M total raised as a proxy for current value and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical for Series B-to-later-stage advancement, yielding an implied valuation of $57M. Peer-median analysis benchmarks against three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies: KoBold Metals at $3.0B (Series C), Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B (Series C), and Amogy at $700M (Series C). The median of this peer set is $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B.

Triangulating these two methods produces a valuation range of $48M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $528M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around Cemvita's technology maturity, addressable market capture potential, and competitive positioning relative to later-stage peers commanding substantially higher valuations. Stage progression anchors conservatively to capital raised, while peer comps reflect sector valuations at more mature development stages.
